resources.string: This phone has 4 GB of RAM. No app can add more. Killing a background app frees RAM now; badly behaved apps will restart and eat it again. If RAM is always full, the fix is fewer heavy apps, not a stronger killer.

No app can create signal that isn\'t there. A flick or a mode lock can make the phone re-attach to a tower that exists — it cannot invent coverage. If both SIMs show no service, the problem is the towers, not the phone.

The DNS pipe blocks junk domains before they load and can be faster than the carrier\'s DNS. It does not make the connection faster, and the first query for a domain is slower. Queries to the chosen upstream are unencrypted in v1.2.
Muse learns about a blast, a SIM pull, or a rogue app only on the next poll. Worst case, the wait is the poll interval. There is no live push in v1.2.
A user who never touches ADB gets a complete v1.2 except one-tap airplane flick and one-tap network-mode lock.

Two features need a one-time grant from a computer: one-tap airplane flick and one-tap network-mode lock. Without them the app shows guided manual steps instead. The grants survive reboots and app updates, and are lost on uninstall — the app re-checks on every launch and will show “re-run ADB setup” if a grant is gone.
DUMP — extra diagnostics (experimental; may unlock nothing usable)
READ_LOGS — DND culprit detection from the system log (experimental)
